items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between calls; each session's context is built from scratch from whatever the program loads, so without a saved store nothing from Monday is available. Window size only limits one conversation; a prompt line cannot create storage.
The page arrives after call 2, so the first call that can include it is call 3. The program re-sends the history each call, so calls 3, 4, 5 and 6 include it.

items.answer: It would be costly, since all that text is re-sent on every call, and a full context can reduce accuracy or may not fit at all.
accepted: too many tokens and worse recall
too costly and the model may miss the relevant part
items.rationale: Any two of: token cost on every call, may exceed the window, context rot making the model less accurate on the relevant part.

An exact permission fact should be written by the program, not left to the model, and loaded at session start. Relying on the model to take a note, on the student's say-so, or on a pasted old chat is unreliable or wasteful.

items.answer: Begin each chunk with the machine name and section heading (add context to the chunk before indexing).
accepted: add the machine name to each chunk
prefix chunks with the manual title
include the machine name in every chunk
items.rationale: Chunks must make sense alone; adding the machine and section as a prefix, as in contextual retrieval, lets search match the right machine.
